text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Sentry ingestion error rate spike and dropped payloads detected for sentry-prod (last 5m). Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

pager-duty-bot: Paging sre-oncall (<@sre-oncall>) for incident #INC-2026-042. Escalation level: page.

sre-oncall: ack — I'm on it. Seeing a 40% drop in accepted events vs expected.

jonas: also seeing increased 502s from the vendor endpoint when we forward envelopes. stack traces are getting truncated. Quick check: are we hitting auth failures or rate limits?

kevin: support queue picks up a handful of customer reports: "no error events in dashboard for my service since 09:12 UTC". Ticket IDs: 5238, 5241.

anita (support): customers are getting timeouts from Sentry SDKs in our agent logs; they're reported as transient but no retries happening currently.

sre-oncall: hypothesis: third-party observability vendor (our Sentry provider) is rate limiting / auth-ing requests from our ingestion proxy. Looking at proxy logs now.

jonas: logs (redacted):

```
2026-03-12T09:14:21Z svc-proxy sentry: POST /api/123/envelope 429 RateLimit reached (header: x-rate-limit-policy=auth)
2026-03-12T09:14:22Z svc-proxy sentry: POST /api/123/envelope 502 Bad Gateway (upstream timeout)
2026-03-12T09:14:23Z svc-proxy sentry: POST /api/123/envelope 401 Unauthorized (token expired)
```

maria (product): what customers are affected? Do we have a map from token -> org?

kevin: yes, mapping shows ~12 orgs on affected token pool, including one large customer doing heavy logging: org-987. They report silence in their monitoring.

sre-oncall: immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Rotate the short-lived token(s) used to forward to vendor (if auth fails).
2) Switch forwarding to our secondary error pipeline (local buffer -> s3 archive + async retry) to avoid loss.
3) Throttle high-volume producers at the proxy and queue their envelopes.
4) Open support case with vendor for rate-limit exception and request emergency quota.

jonas: I can do 1 and 2. Plan: rotate token in the proxy config and enable buffer mode. Doing a canary on one proxy instance first.

sre-oncall: do it. Add config snippet used to enable buffer mode in the agent:

```
# proxy config
sentry_forwarding:
  mode: buffered
  buffer_path: /var/lib/sentry-buffer
  flush_interval_seconds: 60
  max_buffer_mb: 512
```

jonas: canary rollout started: updating proxy pods svc-proxy-3 -> svc-proxy-3-canary.

incident-bot: Deploy (svc-proxy v2.14.1) started by jonas.

sre-oncall: while canary rolls, I'll open the vendor support ticket and request quota info + auth error root cause.

sre-oncall: Vendor support case opened: SENTRY-TICKET-9982 — attaching sample failing envelope and upstream logs.

maria (product): product impact assessment: 12 orgs affected, 2 with severity-high (org-987 and org-102). Potential for missed SLA for error capture. Recommend proactive customer outreach for top two.

kevin: I'll draft messages for org-987 and org-102. For others we'll include a status update in the status page.

anita (support): temporary mitigation note for customers: "If you're not seeing new errors in the dashboard, we are buffering events and will reprocess once upstream recovers. No action needed unless you need immediate alerts; in that case we'll provide a manual webhook to capture critical alerts."

jonas: canary results: buffered mode prevented drops for canary traffic. Token rotate applied; new token accepted by vendor for canary, 200s returned. Rolling update to 30% of proxy fleet.

incident-bot: svc-proxy canary metrics: error forwarding success rate increased from 60% -> 98% on canary.

sre-oncall: rolling to 100% now. Also enabling an emergency rule to throttle large producers to 5 req/s per token to reduce upstream pressure. Config snippet: 

```
# rate limit override
proxy.rate_limit.override:
  enabled: true
  default_rps: 5
  token_whitelist: ["org-admin-token"]
```

jonas: rolled to 100% at 09:22 UTC. Post-rollout monitoring shows drop in 502s and 401s.

sre-oncall: vendor responded: they had an internal deploy causing auth token rotation + a short misconfigured rate-limit. They've reverted and increased quota for our ingress for 15 minutes to catch up. Vendor reference: INC-37721.

maria (product): good. Next steps:
- Confirm buffered events reingested successfully.
- Trigger reprocessing for org-987 and org-102 and confirm sample errors show up.
- Customer comms: send targeted notes to two high-impact customers, status update for others.
- Postmortem and followups with vendor on SLA/alerting.

kevin: customer message drafted and approved by legal. Sending now.

anita (support): customers acknowledged, org-987 confirmed events reappearing at 09:35 UTC.

jonas: reprocessing script used:

```
aws s3 cp s3://sentry-buffer/2026/03/12/org-987/ part-
for f in part-*; do curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotated-token>" --data-binary @${f} https://sentry.vendor/api/123/envelope; done
```

sre-oncall: monitoring shows reingestion backlog cleared by 09:50 UTC. We'll keep buffered mode on for 10 more minutes and then revert to normal forwarding.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 transitioned to mitigated. Postmortem requested and assigned to jonas. ETA: 3 business days.

maria (product): add follow-ups: vendor contract review for burst quota, add alert for upstream 401 spikes and header x-rate-limit-policy presence, automate token rotation detection in the proxy, and a runbook entry for buffered-mode fallback.

jonas: starting postmortem doc draft. High level notes captured; will include timeline, root cause (vendor token rotation + misconfigured rate-limiter), mitigations (rotate tokens, buffered pipeline, throttle), and action items.

kevin: closing customer comms loop. All affected customers confirmed resolution or monitoring.

sre-oncall: #action: jonas to own postmortem. #action: platform team to implement automated health check to detect vendor auth changes. #action: support to send final post-incident summary to affected customers.

pager-duty-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 marked RESOLVED by sre-oncall at 2026-03-12T09:56:00Z.

sre-oncall: thanks everyone. If anyone sees recurring gaps in error signals, ping here.

maria (product): thanks team — good coordination. We'll track vendor follow-ups in the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
